dict/1/p0: A swordsmanship technique where the user draws the blade from the scabbard and strikes the opponent in an instant. Its origins are traced back to the Sengoku period. In modern times, it refers to learning and performing kata rather than actual combat.
dict/1/p1: Since the Kusanagi Shrine enshrines swords, members of the Kusanagi family have a tradition of practicing iai swordsmanship.
dict/2/p0: The supreme god of Greek mythology who rules the sky. He wields lightning as a weapon. He is the father of Apollon and Dionysus, and the younger brother of Hades. In Greek myths, he often transforms into various forms, such as swans or bulls, to trick gods and humans.
dict/3/p0: A space created by Zeus. Gods selected from various mythological worlds were summoned here to learn about humans and love. While the academy is the main facility, Zeus can create anything he desires. Those who remain in the Garden's atmosphere do not age, regardless of how much time passes.
dict/4/p0: Read as "Ame-no-Murakumo-no-Tsurugi." It is considered one of the Three Sacred Treasures and is also known by the alternate name Kusanagi-no-Tsurugi.
dict/4/p1: A sword passed down for generations at the Kusanagi Shrine. It is also what led to {NAME} being summoned to the Garden.
dict/5/p0: Restraints placed on the gods in the Garden to limit their divine powers. Their shapes vary by god, appearing as rings, pendants, etc. They suppress the gods' original powers and natures, and are removed when the gods gain an understanding of humans at the academy. Removing the shackles is the condition for graduation.
dict/6/p0: Refers to the powers and natures that gods inherently possess. There are various types of abilities. Gods in the Garden cannot fully activate their divine abilities due to restrictions imposed by their shackles.
dict/7/p0: The term for the three goddesses of Greek mythology: Atropos, Clotho, and Lachesis. Also known as the Three Fates. They are goddesses of destiny, with Atropos symbolizing "birth," Clotho "spinning," and Lachesis "death," holding the role of monitoring and determining human fate.
dict/8/p0: The Egyptian god of wisdom. Within Egyptian mythology, he is said to have the head of a ibis or a baboon. Thoth is known for holding the caduceus, a staff entwined by two snakes. There is a story that when the two snakes were fighting, placing the staff between them caused them to entwine and stop fighting.
dict/9/p0: Read as "yaoyorozu no kami." This is a unique Japanese concept that a spirit resides in all things. "Yaoyorozu" is not a specific number but indicates a very large quantity. A characteristic example is the "God of the Toilet."
dict/10/p0: The sun god of Greek mythology. In Greek myth, he also presides over prophecy and the arts, and is said to be the most beautiful of the Olympians. Apollo's golden bow and arrows, Aganippe, have the power to heighten the passion of those they strike, and myths featuring Apollo and this weapon are depicted.
dict/11/p0: The Norse god who presides over light. His gentle nature remains prominent even in the myths, and he was widely loved, earning the title "Prince of the Gods." Baldr's ship, Hringhorni, is said to be the largest in the world, and there is a tale in Norse mythology that it was so heavy it could not be moved.
dict/12/p0: The Japanese god who presides over the moon. His formal name is Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto. He is the god who rules over Yoru-no-Oskuni (the Night Land). In ancient times, calendars were counted by the moon, so he was also worshipped as the god of calendars. He is the brother of Amaterasu and Susanoo.
dict/13/p0: The god of the underworld in Greek mythology. Since he causes grains to sprout underground and generate wealth, he is also called Plouton, meaning "the wealthy one." He is often referred to by the epithet "King of the Underworld" and is widely feared by both gods and humans. He possesses the Helm of Hades, which renders the wearer invisible, and this helm plays an active role in Greek mythology.
dict/14/p0: The Greek god who presides over wine. He is also called Bacchus and is worshipped as the god of fertility and theater. In Greek mythology, there are many stories related to grapes, and in paintings, he is often depicted holding a thyrsus, a staff wrapped in grapevines.
dict/17/p0: The Japanese god who governs the sea. His formal title is Susanoo-no-Mikoto. Along with Amaterasu and Tsukuyomi, the three are collectively known as the Three Noble Children (Sankishi). He is said to have composed the first Japanese waka poem, with the verse "Yakumo tatsu Izumo yae-gaki tsumigomi ni yae-gaki tsukuru sono yae-gaki o" being passed down.
dict/18/p0: A notebook containing school rules, maps of the Garden, and other information. Its contents are updated at Zeus's whim. Presenting the Student Handbook at the Canteen allows you to receive items of your choice.
dict/19/p0: A shop located within the school. It features a wide variety of goods and is operated by the Greek god Hermes alongside the dolls created by Zeus. Students can receive desired items by presenting their Student Handbook.
dict/20/p0: The Greek god of commerce. In mythology, he served as the messenger for Zeus, who rules the sky, and Hades, who rules the underworld, and also had a side as an inventor. The lyre held by Apollon was originally made by Hermes.
dict/20/p1: In the Garden, the Canteen is run by leveraging the abilities of the god of commerce.
dict/21/p0: Refers to a state of being unadorned and simple. It is one of the concepts valued in Japanese culture, such as in the tea ceremony.
dict/21/p1: Balder mistakenly remembered wabi-sabi as "wasabi." They are completely different things despite being only one character apart.
dict/22/p0: Balder's mother, the Norse goddess of fertility. She possessed the ability to foresee the future but was said to never speak her visions aloud.
dict/23/p0: A legendary creature. Its Japanese name is fushichou. It resembles a pheasant with reddish-purple plumage, its neck covered in golden feathers. It is said to burst into flames and perish when its life ends, only to be reborn from its ashes. Found in European and Middle Eastern legends, some theories suggest it originated from the Egyptian phoenix, Bennu.
dict/24/p0: A legendary creature. Its Japanese name is ikkajuu. It has a horse-like body with a single horn on its forehead. While appearing in myths worldwide, "unicorn" specifically refers to the Western version, distinguished from the Eastern unicorn, Qilin.
dict/25/p0: A clay doll born when Zeus tried to create humans. She talks like an old Edo townsperson. She usually lives in the dollhouse in {NAME}'s room, and has a surprising fondness for love stories and sake.
dict/26/p0: A place visited by the deceased. Though named differently, it exists in every mythology, often called the underworld or Yomi. The Land of the Dead is a subterranean world; if the living eat its food, they usually cannot return to the surface.
dict/27/p0: A Greek hero. Born human, he endured numerous hardships before being recognized as a god. It is said that the monster he fought became the constellation Leo.
dict/28/p0: A term referring to three prominent stars visible in the spring night sky: Arcturus, Spica, and Denebola. Also called the Spring Triangle. Arcturus is in Bootes, Spica in Virgo, and Denebola in Leo. Besides the Spring Triangle, there are also the Summer Triangle and Winter Triangle.
dict/29/p0: The god of the sea in Greek mythology. He is Hades's younger brother and Zeus's older brother. He wields a three-pronged spear called a trident and is said to stir up the seas and cause great storms when angered.
dict/30/p0: A term for those who do not belong to any specific club and go straight home after school. ...That is the original meaning, but in the Garden, it seems that just having "club" in the name is enough to establish it as a proper club activity.
dict/31/p0: The guard dog of the underworld. It has three heads and a snake's tail. In Greek mythology, its saliva dripping onto the ground is poisonous, and those who see its terrifying appearance are said to turn to stone.
dict/31/p1: The Cerberus in the Garden is very attached to Hades.
dict/33/p0: A divine ability possessed by Apollon. It allows him to know the future, but he cannot know things related to himself.
dict/33/p1: When in human form, it cannot be fully activated, so its accuracy decreases.
dict/34/p0: The star of Aquarius. Sadalsuud means "the happiest star."
dict/34/p1: In this case, it refers to the name Hades gave a turtle when he became the biology teacher. Hades calls it "Sada," giving it an old-fashioned feel.
dict/35/p0: A city-state in Greek mythology. Also called Ilium or Ilion. It was once thought to be fictional, but later investigations revealed it likely existed.
dict/36/p0: A princess of Troy. In Greek mythology, she received the gift of prophecy from Apollon, but her warnings were ignored during the Trojan War, leading to defeat.
dict/37/p0: The ten-year war between Zeus's father, Cronus, and Zeus. Fearing he would be overthrown by his children, Cronus swallowed them one by one. Zeus, who was not swallowed, waged war to save his siblings. The Titanomachy ended when Zeus and his siblings defeated Cronus.
dict/38/p0: An evergreen tree in the palm family. It has no branches and its surface is covered in a fiber-like skin. It blooms with small, grain-like yellow flowers. Apollon and his twin sister Artemis were born under a date palm on the island of Delos.
dict/39/p0: The place where the dead are judged. Also called the underworld or hell. Hades is sometimes called the "King of the Underworld" because he rules it in Greek mythology.
dict/40/p0: Food enjoyed with alcohol. Melissa likes to eat them often, especially smoked squid. She mispronounces "tsumami" as "tsumame" and "sakeika" as "sakeika," though she believes she is pronouncing them correctly.
dict/41/p0: The realm of the dead in Greek mythology. In a narrower sense, it can refer to the deepest part of the underworld. Cerberus, the watchdog, guards the entrance to Tartarus, and Charon, the ferryman, waits by the river inside. He will transport souls to the other side in exchange for a fare. Living humans are blocked by Cerberus at the entrance, so they cannot enter Tartarus.
dict/42/p0: A princess of Ethiopia. Her mother, Cassiopeia, offended Poseidon with her boastful remarks, leading to Andromeda being sacrificed to a sea monster. Perseus rescued her at the last moment, and they were eventually united in marriage.
dict/43/p0: A prince of Argos. On his way back after slaying Medusa, the monster whose gaze turns people to stone, he encountered Andromeda in crisis and saved her. Though he was nearly deceived by her uncle, he overcame the obstacle and united with Andromeda.
dict/44/p0: A divine drink in Greek mythology that grants immortality. It was served alongside ambrosia, the food of the gods, during banquets and gatherings.
dict/45/p0: The goddess of the hearth in Greek mythology. She is the sister of Zeus. The name "Hestia" means "hearth," and she is often confused with Vesta, the Roman goddess of the hearth.
dict/46/p0: The sun deity in Japanese mythology. Her formal name is Amaterasu-Omikami, and she is often depicted as a goddess in myths. She rules over Takamagahara, the celestial world where the gods reside.
dict/47/p0: Read as "Yomi-no-kuni." It is the land of the dead in Japanese mythology, said to be located underground. In the myths, Izanami, who descended to Yomi-no-kuni, ate its food and her body decayed, turning her into a terrifying form.
dict/48/p0: Read as "Takamagahara." In Japanese mythology, it is the world where the gods live. It is said to have existed before the birth of the gods, and after Izanagi and Izanami created the Ashihara-no-Nakatsukuni (the Central Land of Reed Plains), Amaterasu came to rule over it.
dict/49/p0: Read as "Yoru no Osukuni." It is the world of night ruled by Tsukuyomi. The character "Osu" in the name means "to rule."
dict/50/p0: The activation of a god's abilities. It manifests when their shackles are removed or when their emotions are stirred by some event. Upon transforming into their divine form, they revert to their appearance from the mythological world rather than retaining the human guise they maintained in the Garden.
dict/51/p0: A sport in which two people face off using bamboo swords. Originally intended for killing enemies, it is now enjoyed as a sport by people of all ages.
dict/52/p0: A monster from Japanese mythology. In the myths, it has red eyes like a lantern and possesses eight heads and eight tails, with a body as large as eight mountains. It is famous for being slain by Susanoo.
dict/53/p0: A collective term for the Ame-no-Murakumo Sword, the Yata no Kagami mirror, and the Yasakani no Magatama jewel. These were bestowed by Amaterasu when Ninigi-no-Mikoto descended to Earth. They are real objects and are still enshrined today.
dict/55/p0: Read as "Totsuka-no-Tsurugi." The name comes from the fact that the blade is ten fists long (about 90 cm). The Totsuka Sword was owned by Susanoo and is also known as Ame-no-Ohabari or Itsu-no-Ohabari. Its original owner was Susanoo's father, Izanagi.
dict/56/p0: A method of bringing misfortune through spiritual power. While mostly intentional, curses can also be cast unconsciously. Curses are said to carry high risks, symbolized by the proverb "curse someone and you dig two graves for yourself," warning that a failed curse may rebound upon the caster.
dict/57/p0: The seasons in the Garden are determined by Zeus's dice. They don't necessarily follow the spring, summer, autumn, winter order; instead, the season deemed most suitable for the moment is chosen, though the truth behind this is uncertain.
dict/58/p0: The World Tree symbolizing the Norse mythological realm. Yggdrasil is a colossal tree whose branches span the nine worlds of Norse mythology, serving as a symbol of life. Its roots divide into three major branches, extending to the sacred "Well of Urd," the "Well of Mimir" of knowledge, and the "Well of Hvergelmir," source of all poisons.
dict/59/p0: Three consecutive winters of extreme cold, also known as the "Great Winter." The first is the "Winter of Winds," the second the "Winter of Swords," and the third the "Winter of Wolves." During this time, blizzards rage continuously. It is said to be a harbinger of the final battle in Norse mythology.
dict/60/p0: A house made of snow or ice. While similar in shape to a Japanese kamakura, its construction differs: blocks of snow or ice are cut into squares and stacked. The interior of an igloo is lined with branches or fur to keep out the cold.
dict/61/p0: Refers to Kongming lanterns, also known as sky lanterns. These are small hot air balloons made of a bamboo frame with a paper bag placed upside down over it. The cute name "Komkom" came from Apollon's vague memory.
dict/62/p0: The only plant in the Norse mythological world capable of harming Balder. This is because Frigg, Balder's mother, sought oaths from all things to protect him, but spared the young mistletoe sapling, deeming it too harmless.
dict/63/p0: A primer on poetry authored by the Icelandic poet Snorri Sturluson. It compiles Norse myths, folktales, and ancient poems. There are two texts referred to as 'Eddas' in Norse mythology: the 'Prose Edda' (Snorri's Edda), compiled by Snorri from original sources, and the 'Poetic Edda', which adds ancient poems to the original texts.
dict/64/p0: Refers to Jormungandr, the World Serpent. A massive snake in Norse mythology large enough to encircle the world. Its movements cause tsunamis, and its breath is said to be deadly poison. It is depicted as Thor's natural enemy.
dict/65/p0: In Norse mythology, beings that mirror the gods. Giants possess power rivaling the gods and have brought harm to both gods and humans. Their appearances vary widely, from those indistinguishable from humans to giants, and some are exceptionally beautiful.
dict/66/p0: The final battle in Norse mythology. A war where gods and giants fought for each other's survival, also known as the 'Twilight of the Gods.' After this battle, everything sinks to the bottom of the sea, but the sunken land rises again, and a new world is created.
dict/67/p0: The realm where Norse gods reside. Primarily inhabited by Odin, the supreme god, and the Aesir tribe. Thor's hall, Bilskirnir, has 530 rooms, while in Odin's hall, Valhalla, warriors train daily. The roots of Yggdrasil extend into the Well of Urd.
dict/68/p0: Giants from Norse mythology. They are also called Surs, Ris, Trolls, and other names. The realm where giants live in Norse mythology is called Jotunheim, existing like a wall around Midgard, the human realm.
dict/69/p0: The god of death in Egyptian mythology. In myths, he oversees the judgment of the dead in the underworld. Anubis places the deceased's heart on one side of a scale and a feather symbolizing order on the other. If the heart is lighter than the feather, the deceased can return to the living world. Thoth records this ritual.
dict/70/p0: In Egyptian mythology, it is called the "Ba." It is said to reside in the heart that Anubis weighs during judgment. The weight of this heart represents the weight of the soul, and it is said that a good soul becomes lighter.
dict/71/p0: A concept in Egyptian mythology representing justice and order. Its meaning is broad, encompassing proper conduct, correct thinking, and social etiquette. Additionally, the name of the goddess who represents order in Egyptian mythology is also Maat.
dict/72/p0: A spiritual double separate from the physical body. It is often paired with the "Ba," which carries the meaning of soul. In ancient Egypt, statues and figurines were placed around tombs as places for the Ka, which had lost its physical body.
dict/73/p0: A dried corpse. Written as "mumi" in kanji. In ancient Egypt, mummies were created by removing internal organs and drying the body to preserve the deceased.
dict/74/p0: A phrase symbolizing the human impulse to do what is forbidden. By extension, it refers to actual fruits like apples or grapes. Such stories are also called "the Taboo of Eden," and similar parables can be found all over the world.
dict/75/p0: The god of time in Greek mythology and the father of Hades and Zeus. Fearing a prophecy that he would be overthrown by his own children, he swallowed them one by one, but was deposed by Zeus, who escaped Cronus's grasp. While Cronus is said to have been a ruthless tyrant, there is also the opposite theory that he was a gentle and compassionate king, revealing a multifaceted side to his rule as a monarch.
dict/76/p0: The twelve principal gods of Greek mythology. Zeus, Apollon, Hermes, and Dionysus are among them, though the exact members vary by source and era.
dict/77/p0: Corn. Thoth calls it the "golden crop" and claims it is the supreme food. If you bring up corn with Thoth, you are guaranteed to be detained for five hours.
dict/78/p0: The school library's collection spans everything from books on gods and mythology to practical guides, though some titles might make you scratch your head. Thoth has essentially turned the library into his personal space, and he lives there with Anubis.
dict/79/p0: A mythological system developed near the Nile River in Egypt. A distinctive feature of Egyptian mythology is its strong element of animal worship. Reflecting this, many gods in Egyptian mythology are depicted with animal heads. In mythology, Anubis is shown with the head of a black dog, and Thoth with the head of an ibis or a baboon.
dict/80/p0: A plan aimed at fostering harmony between gods and humans. Proposed by Zeus and the principal gods of the world, it intends to deepen mutual understanding by having gods and humans attend school together.
dict/15/p0: The Norse god who presides over fire. He is known as the trickster of Norse mythology. Famous for his mischief and troublemaking, he also shows a side as an inventor. The sword Revathain has runes inscribed on its blade, and it was forged by Loki.
dict/16/p0: The Norse god who presides over thunder. In Norse mythology, he is often depicted as a burly, powerful man. Despite being a god, he shows a gentle side by siding with humans. Megingjord is a belt that doubles Thor's strength, and he wore it at his waist, playing an active role in the mythological world.
dict/32/p0: A tale found in the Kojiki and the Inaba Country Fudoki, also widely passed down as a folk tale. Once, a rabbit was punished for deceiving a crocodile and had its fur stripped off. Passersby, the brothers of Okuninushi, told it to bathe in saltwater and expose itself to the wind to heal, which the rabbit did. However, the pain only intensified. Eventually, Okuninushi passed by, told the rabbit to wash its body with fresh water, rub it with cattail pollen, and lie down to recover. Grateful, the rabbit helped Okuninushi find a bride, and since then, the white rabbit of Inaba has been regarded as a god of matchmaking.
dict/54/p0: Tools used in Shinto rituals. These are sakaki branches or white wooden rods adorned with shide (paper streamers). Shinto priests use them to purify sins and impurities. Onusa represents the garments of the gods, and a new one is used each time it is employed.
